sec: Thyroid storm, neonatal thyrotoxicosis, surgery complications

items.q: Match the following thyroid-storm feature — 1) Trigger 2) Burch-Wartofsky component 3) First-line thionamide 4) Adjunct … A) Infection / surgery / trauma B) Score ≥ 45 suggests storm C) Propylthiouracil D) Iodine (≥1 h after thionamide) + beta-blocker + steroid
items.exp: Triggers include infection, surgery and trauma; Burch-Wartofsky ≥ 45 suggests storm; PTU is preferred in storm; iodine is given at least one hour after thionamide along with beta-blocker and steroid. (Book p913)

items.q: A patient with Graves disease post-appendicectomy has fever 39.5 °C, HR 158/min, agitation and jaundice. The most likely diagnosis is:
items.exp: High fever, tachyarrhythmia, agitation and jaundice after a precipitating event in Graves fit thyroid storm. (Book p913)

items.q: Assess thyroid storm management: I Iodine should precede the thionamide. II IV hydrocortisone is part of the regimen.
items.exp: Iodine is given at least one hour after the thionamide to avoid substrate for new hormone; hydrocortisone covers possible adrenal insufficiency and reduces T4-to-T3 conversion. (Book p913)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a treatment used in thyroid storm?
items.exp: PTU, propranolol and hydrocortisone are standard; lithium is not standard storm therapy (it can be adjunct in severe cases but not routine). (Book p913)

items.q: The Burch-Wartofsky score ≥ ___ suggests thyroid storm.
items.exp: A score of 45 or more on the Burch-Wartofsky scale is highly suggestive of thyroid storm. (Book p913)

items.q: Match the following context — 1) Neonatal thyrotoxicosis 2) Postpartum Graves 3) Subclinical thyrotoxicosis 4) Apathetic thyrotoxicosis … A) Transplacental TRAb; treat with thionamide B) May flare after delivery C) TSH < 0.1 with normal free hormones D) Elderly with apathy rather than hyperactivity
items.exp: Neonatal thyrotoxicosis is from transplacental TRAb; postpartum Graves may flare after delivery; subclinical thyrotoxicosis has low TSH with normal free hormones; apathetic thyrotoxicosis presents with apathy in elderly. (Book p913)

items.q: A neonate born to a mother with active Graves disease has tachycardia, irritability and poor weight gain. The most appropriate therapy is:
items.exp: Neonatal thyrotoxicosis is treated with thionamide (methimazole preferred after first weeks) plus a beta-blocker; iodide can be added. (Book p913)

items.q: Assess neonatal thyrotoxicosis: I It is caused by transplacental TSH-receptor antibodies. II It typically resolves as maternal antibodies clear over weeks.
items.exp: Maternal TRAb crosses the placenta; symptoms resolve over weeks to months as antibodies wane. (Book p913)

items.q: Match the following surgical complication of thyroidectomy — 1) Hypoparathyroidism 2) Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury 3) Haematoma with airway compromise 4) Hypothyroidism … A) Hypocalcaemia with tetany B) Hoarseness / stridor C) Emergency airway decompression D) Expected after total thyroidectomy
items.exp: Hypoparathyroidism causes hypocalcaemia and tetany; recurrent laryngeal nerve injury causes hoarseness or stridor; neck haematoma is an airway emergency; hypothyroidism is expected after total thyroidectomy. (Book p913)

items.q: A patient has stridor and a tense neck haematoma within hours of thyroidectomy. The next step is:
opts: Emergency wound decompression at the bedside
CT scan of the neck before intervention
items.exp: Post-thyroidectomy haematoma with airway compromise requires immediate opening of the wound at the bedside before definitive airway. (Book p913)

items.q: Bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve injury post-thyroidectomy can cause ___.
opts: Bilateral vocal-cord paralysis and airway obstruction
items.exp: Bilateral injury causes vocal-cord paralysis in the adducted position and acute airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy. (Book p913)

items.q: Assess surgery in Graves: I Total thyroidectomy achieves rapid control. II It is preferred in patients with active moderate ophthalmopathy.
items.exp: Total thyroidectomy rapidly controls hyperthyroidism and is preferred in active ophthalmopathy to avoid RAI-induced flare. (Book p913)
